questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes a primary function of most Nigerian traditional arts before modern times?
options: They were made strictly to be sold to European tourists.
They were produced mainly for public art galleries.
They served religious, cultural, and royal ceremonial purposes.
They were used primarily as teaching tools for school children.
questions.explain: Nigerian traditional art was heavily functional. Artworks served religious purposes (shrines, ancestral worship), cultural documentation, and highlighted the power of traditional rulers.

questions.q: In traditional Nigerian societies, figures carved specifically to represent ancestors or deities are mainly utilized in:
options: Commercial trading
Shrines and religious worship
Farming practices
Building construction
questions.explain: Sculptures and carvings that represented deities or ancestors were typically placed in shrines and utilized as focal points for traditional religious worship and rituals.

questions.q: Which ancient Nigerian traditional art culture was accidentally discovered by a man digging a well or cistern in his compound?
options: Esie stone figures
Nok terracotta
Benin bronzes
Igbo-Ukwu art
questions.explain: Igbo-Ukwu artifacts were accidentally discovered in 1938 by a local man named Isaiah Anozie while digging a cistern in his compound in Anambra State.

questions.q: In traditional Nigerian societies, an ornately carved wooden staff was most likely used as a:
options: Child's toy for entertainment.
Tool to dig soil for farming.
Symbol of authority, spiritual power, or royal status.
Standardized ruler for measuring fabric.
questions.explain: Functional items like carved staffs, stools, and flywhisks were deeply symbolic in traditional society, primarily functioning to represent the spiritual and temporal authority of chiefs, kings, or priests.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a 'Court Art' in the context of traditional Nigerian history (such as the art of Benin)?
options: Artworks used exclusively by farmers during the harvest festival.
Artworks designed and owned exclusively by the King (Oba) and his royal household to display prestige and document history.
Artworks created for the modern judicial courts to decorate legal chambers.
Artworks sold randomly in local street markets.
questions.explain: Court art refers to artworks commissioned, controlled, and used exclusively by the monarchy (the court) to reinforce the king's power, spiritual authority, and to record historical royal events.
